title: Designing CLIs for Agents, Not Humans — Pedro Lopez, Airbyte
talk_summary: Airbyte built an MCP server and a CLI as thin presentational layers over their platform APIs, driven by an OpenAPI spec, and learned that agent-facing interfaces need JSON in/out, strict noun-verb consistency, small tool counts with progressive discovery, and no interactive prompts. They also ship a skill alongside the CLI so agents can discover it, and split skill content into reference files to limit context load.

takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of human-style flags, the CLI accepts a JSON payload and emits JSON, so agents construct inputs directly and pipe output through jq/head/tail.
takeaways.evidence_quote: take JSON in and return JSON out ... agents are really good at working with JSON

takeaways.technique: Noun-verb consistency as an agent contract
takeaways.what_they_do: Every resource follows the same `noun verb` shape (connectors list, connectors create, workspace list), and repeated agent mistakes are treated as a signal to change the contract, not the prompt.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you see agents making the same mistake over and over ... consider making that your contract

takeaways.what_they_do: Rather than one tool per entity/action, they expose two tools (describe schema, execute) and let the agent discover capabilities incrementally, keeping tool descriptions short.

takeaways.technique: Ship a skill with the tool, split into references
takeaways.what_they_do: A skill file is installed alongside the CLI so agents can discover it exists; the main skill points to reference files that expand per-command detail only when needed.

takeaways.technique: No interactive prompts in agent-invoked tools
takeaways.what_they_do: Because no human is present, credentials and choices must come via flags, env vars, or config files set out of band; interactive prompts make agents hang.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it can't sit there and wait for you to type ... you have to expose things either through flags ... environment variables and config files

takeaways.technique: OpenAPI spec as single source of truth
takeaways.what_they_do: Interfaces are thin presentational layers generated on top of shared OpenAPI specs, so they stay current as the platform deploys many times a day.
takeaways.numbers: platform changes over 10 times a day
